content.text: {"decision":"YES","supporting_policy_ids":["E01","E02","E03","E04","E05","E06","E07","E08","E09","E10","E11","E12","E13"],"missing_facts":[],"justification":"All Gift Aid requirements are met for payment FP-0316-EL (Elaine Carter's £120 direct bank transfer on 16 March 2026). (1) The charity is HMRC-recognised as of 16 March 2026 [E02]. (2) Elaine is an individual donor [E06]. (3) She has a signed Gift Aid declaration covering this payment [E05]. (4) Her Income Tax paid for 2025–26 is £980, which comfortably exceeds the £80 total Gift Aid being claimed across all her donations that year (£120 × 25p = £30 for this donation alone), satisfying the tax-paid threshold [E04/E07]. (5) None of the exclusions apply: the payment was not made via Payroll Giving [E09], was not a payment for goods or services and Elaine received no benefit [E10/E11], was not a share transfer [E12], and was not from a charity card or CAF voucher — it was a direct bank transfer with its own settlement reference [E13]. The charity can therefore claim 25p per £1 donated, i.e. £30 Gift Aid on this £120 donation [E01].","scope_issues":["The question is answered specifically for payment FP-0316-EL (Elaine Carter). Other monthly direct debit donors and one-off donors would each need to satisfy the same individual eligibility criteria (HMRC-recognised charity, valid Gift Aid declaration, sufficient Income Tax/CGT paid, no excluded payment type) before Gift Aid can be claimed on their donations."],"conditional_branches":[]}
